When the


[restaurant industry](https://ottimate.com/industry/restaurants/) pulls back on hiring, back office teams are among the first to feel the pain. Finance and accounting roles are frequently consolidated or left unfilled, yet invoice volume and supplier complexity continue to grow.


For lean finance teams, the workload doesn't go away simply because there are fewer people available to handle it. Instead, it gets pushed to the employees who are still around. Stretched teams become overwhelmed by manual work, creating opportunities for errors that impact the bottom line.


In this hiring environment, accounts payable automation is becoming an operational necessity, enabling smaller finance teams to keep up with growing workloads without increasing financial risk.


## The hiring slowdown is hitting the back office


Hiring challenges in the restaurant industry are often discussed in the context of front-of-house staff. But finance teams are feeling the pressure, too. As restaurant groups look for opportunities to control costs amid ongoing economic uncertainty, many are keeping accounting and AP roles vacant longer or reassigning responsibilities to existing staff.


But while finance teams are getting smaller, workloads aren’t following suit. A


[recent survey](https://ottimate.com/resources/ap-maturity-report-2026/) found that nearly half of hospitality businesses process more than 5,000 invoices each month, and 28% say it takes 5 or more days to process just one invoice. Those invoices come from hundreds of suppliers, in varying formats, and through different channels. The complexity only continues to grow as restaurants expand to new locations and add new menu offerings.


When fewer people are responsible for managing the same heavy volume of invoices, teams struggle to keep pace while maintaining accuracy. Invoice processing takes longer, or errors slip through more often. Sometimes, it’s both. This widens the gap between expected and actual food costs, making it harder for finance teams to understand where margin is being lost and what they should do to prevent small issues from becoming bigger problems.


## When one person is covering multiple roles


When finance teams get smaller, the remaining people absorb the work. Often, that means one person is responsible for work that was once split across two or three people. For example, a controller who once focused on financial oversight may now be bogged down by coding invoices, matching purchase orders, and chasing down


[approvals](https://ottimate.com/blog/five-signs-your-approval-workflow-needs-an-upgrade/) . Or an AP manager responsible for strategic improvements may spend countless hours on manual data entry and exception handling just to keep invoices on track.


The drain on the remaining employees’ time is the obvious impact. It’s no secret that managing more responsibilities takes more time. But perhaps the more concerning cost is what


*doesn’t* get done. Duplicate invoices, price creep, expired promotional pricing, and early payment discounts can easily be missed when staff doesn’t have any time left to spend looking for them.


A lean finance team isn’t necessarily a problem. The problem is expecting that smaller team to manage growing invoice volume and complexity using manual processes built for a much larger team.


## How automation changes the equation


Automation will never replace human finance professionals, but it can significantly impact how they spend their time. Specifically, it significantly reduces the manual, repetitive work that drains their time, allowing them to focus on higher-value responsibilities.


Instead of manually entering invoice data, coding GL accounts, or matching invoices to purchase orders, finance teams can automate much of the routine processing that burns up their time. Approval workflows automatically route invoices to the right people, keeping them on track even with smaller teams.


Automation can also help lean teams identify issues they might otherwise miss. For example, automation can detect duplicate invoices before payment is made and flag discrepancies in real time. Instead of manually reviewing thousands of invoices each month, finance teams can focus on the ones that truly require human judgment.


In short, automation enables restaurant finance teams to keep up with growing invoice volume and complexity without a proportional increase in manual work. In a slow hiring season when adding headcount isn't always possible, this gives restaurants a practical way to increase AP capacity while maintaining control and freeing existing finance teams to focus on higher-value work.


## Building a more resilient finance operation


Restaurant hiring may eventually rebound, but shrinking finance teams can’t afford to wait around for that to happen. If they do, efficiency, accuracy, and control are all likely to take a hit.


As invoice volume and complexity continue to increase, manual AP processes become less sustainable. Automation gives lean finance teams the capacity to support business growth, improve financial controls, and focus on work that truly requires human judgment. For restaurant groups under pressure to do more with less, building that operational capacity is critical for long-term success.
